 Dylan Harper 
 SAS 
 Guard 
 #2 
 Player Stats
 Link copied to clipboard! 
 Dylan Harper recorded 22 points (9-of-18 FGs, 1-of-1 FTs), five rebounds, two assists, two steals and three three-pointers in Saturday’s win over the Mavericks.
 Harper’s first three games have gone well for him individually, even though the Spurs are just 1-2 this season. Against the Mavericks, he posted a season-high point total and recorded his first two steals. The Spurs’ rotation still isn’t whole because of Tobias Harris’ strained calf, but Harper’s place in the starting lineup appears secure. 
 -  Raphielle Johnson

 Tobias Harris (calf) is out for Friday’s game against the Rockets. 
 Harris, whose calf strain sidelined him for the entire preseason, will miss a second consecutive regular-season game. His absence means Dylan Harper and Devin Vassell will continue to start, and that may remain true even after Harris returns to action. 
 Dylan Harper 
 SAS 
 Guard 
 #2 
 Dylan Harper contributed 18 points (7-of-17 FGs), seven rebounds and five assists against the Thunder on Tuesday. 
 Harper got the starting nod as part of the three-guard lineup for San Antonio, and he was able to have a productive night in 32 minutes. There were certainly some holes to his fantasy game, most notably the shooting percentage and lack of defensive stats. However, he was able to flash why the organization is so high on him. If Harper remains a starter against the Rockets on Friday, he should be in for another productive night. 
 Victor Wembanyama 
 SAS 
 Forward-Center 
 #1 
 The San Antonio Spurs will start DeAaron Fox, Stephon Castle, Dylan Harper, Devin Vassell, and Victor Wembanyama on Friday against the Kings. 
 Jeff McDonald also reported that coach Mitch Johnson intends to use this starting lineup on Tuesday against the Thunder. The Spurs will use their three guard lineup with Champagnie and Harris coming off the bench. We’ll see if the starting lineup sticks that way beyond this upcoming Tuesday, but you can feel good to draft Vassell to stream him in on opening night. 
 Dylan Harper 
 SAS 
 Guard 
 #2 
 Dylan Harper finished Wednesday’s exhibition against the Suns with nine points (4-of-11 FGs), six rebounds, one assist and one three-pointer. 
 With Julian Champagnie getting the night off, Harper remained in the starting five despite De’Aaron Fox making his first appearance of the preseason. Whether he starts or comes off the bench, Harper has a high fantasy ceiling heading into his second NBA season. The top-100 ADP is reasonable, as Harper will play plenty for the reigning Western Conference champions. With the Spurs playing their final preseason game on Friday, we should get a more definitive answer on Mitch Johnson’s starting lineup then. 
 Dylan Harper 
 SAS 
 Guard 
 #2 
 Dylan Harper tallied 16 points (5-of-7 FGs, 3-of-4 FTs), four rebounds, four assists, one steal and three three-pointers in Thursday’s exhibition against the Hawks. 
 De’Aaron Fox was unavailable for Thursday’s exhibition, so Harper started. The second-year guard played well in 19 minutes, shooting well and committing no turnovers. Even if he’s asked to come off the bench again this season, Harper can provide top-100 fantasy value. At a minimum, his playing time should increase, as he averaged 22.6 minutes per game as a rookie. 
 Dylan Harper 
 SAS 
 Guard 
 #2 
 Dylan Harper finished Saturday’s Game 5 loss to the Knicks with 25 points (10-of-19 FGs, 3-of-5 FTs), five rebounds, four assists, one block and two three-pointers. 
 Harper was San Antonio’s best player in Game 5, and his lack of opportunities in the fourth quarter contributed to the Spurs’ inability to hold off the Knicks. A similar scenario occurred in Game 4, and Harper is the first rookie since Richard Dumas in 1993 to record consecutive 20-point games. After the defeat, teammate Devin Vassell said that there were times during the season when Harper was frustrated with his playing time. Given how well he played during San Antonio’s run to the Finals, minutes should not be a concern for Harper in 2026-27. Don’t be surprised if he breaks out next season. 
 Dylan Harper 
 SAS 
 Guard 
 #2 
 Dylan Harper amassed 21 points (8-of-12 FGs, 2-of-2 FTs), four rebounds, three assists and three three-pointers in the loss to the Knicks on Wednesday. 
 Harper logged another impactful performance on San Antonio’s bench in Game 4. He led the team with a plus-12 rating and finished as one of two Spurs players with 20 or more points. The rookie recorded double-digit points in six consecutive playoff games at the conclusion of Wednesday’s game. He continues to log heavy minutes and will likely see another heavy workload on Saturday. 
 Dylan Harper 
 SAS 
 Guard 
 #2 
 Dylan Harper provided a boost off the bench with 13 points (5-of-18 FGs), nine rebounds, four assists and one three-pointer in Game 3 against the Knicks on Monday. 
 The rookie has been incredible throughout the postseason, though he wasn’t able to match his shooting efficiency in this game. It was a rough shooting night for Harper, but that didn’t prevent the Spurs from securing their first win of the series. He’s been important to the team’s success, which isn’t common for a 20-year-old in the NBA Finals. The volume will increase as he ages, which should lead to some incredible fantasy seasons. For now, he’ll look to make an impact in his role as the series continues on Thursday. 
 Stephon Castle 
 SAS 
 Guard 
 #5 
 Stephon Castle (ankle) said on Sunday that his right ankle is “feeling good” ahead of Monday’s Game 3 of the NBA Finals against the Knicks. 
 Castle appeared to injure his right leg during the second half of Game 2 on Friday. While he did exit the game shortly after the tweak, the second-year guard was back on the court in the fourth quarter as the Spurs rallied. Based on Castle’s comments on Sunday, he should be a full go for Game 3 as the Spurs look to cut the Knicks’ 2-0 lead in half. “It’s been feeling good,” Castle said. “It feels a lot better than I thought it would initially. Obviously, I had some adrenaline running, kind of once I settled down, I started to feel it. Waking up the next day, actually felt really good.” Castle was not listed on the injury report released by the Spurs on Sunday afternoon, so he’ll take on his usual starting role. 
 Dylan Harper 
 SAS 
 Guard 
 #2 
 Dylan Harper had 18 points (6-of-9 FGs, 4-of-4 FTs), six rebounds, four assists and two three-pointers in Thursday’s win over the Thunder in Game 6. 
 Harper’s 18 points in 22 minutes off the bench were absolutely crucial for the Spurs in Game 6. The 20-year-old guard scored more points than any individual player on the Thunder. Harper continues to impress with his play in the playoffs as he’s played beyond his years. Saturday’s Game 7 on the road will surely be his most difficult test yet.

 Trae Young amassed 25 points (6-of-13 FGs, 9-of-9 FTs), four rebounds, nine assists and four three-pointers in Saturday’s win over the Bulls.
 Young’s point total has increased in each of his first three games this season, and his efficiency improved on Saturday. In addition to the improved field-goal percentage, the Wizards’ point guard committed just two turnovers in 34 minutes. For most of Young’s career, fantasy managers have had to punt the turnover category. Over three games, he’s recorded 34 assists and eight turnovers, a very good ratio. The Wizards play three games in Week 2, starting with the Hornets on Monday.

 Jalen Johnson led the Hawks with 26 points (8-of-19 FGs, 8-of-10 FTs), nine rebounds, 16 assists, two steals and two three-pointers in a 121-114 loss to the Rockets on Saturday.
 The Hawks dropped a game for the first time this season, but Johnson was still fantastic for fantasy managers. His field goal percentage was subpar, but the near triple-double made up for it, especially since he matched his career high for assists. Johnson’s shooting percentage has been rough in two of Atlanta’s three games so far, but he is currently averaging a triple-double, which has allowed him to be one of the best players in fantasy basketball to this point.
 -  Noah Rubin

 Amen Thompson recorded a double-double on Saturday with 17 points (4-of-12 FGs, 9-of-9 FTs), 11 rebounds, five assists and one steal in a 121-114 win over the Hawks.
 Three games into the season, Thompson has three double-doubles. While that has been great for fantasy managers, it was the free throw shooting that stuck out. After shooting 3-of-5 in the opener, he has shot 10-of-10 over the last two games. Last season, he shot 77.9 percent from the floor after shooting 68.4 percent in each of his first two seasons. Any continued improvement will only make him more dangerous in fantasy basketball.
 -  Noah Rubin

 Zaccharie Risacher recorded 11 points (4-of-8 FGs, 2-of-2 FTs), four rebounds, two assists, one steal, two blocks and one three-pointer in Saturday’s loss to the Spurs.
 After Cooper Flagg sustained a left shoulder injury in Friday’s win over the Pacers, Risacher started for the Mavericks for the first time on Saturday. He had a highlight-worthy block on Victor Wembanyama at the rim in the first half, but his overall production wasn’t enough to put Risacher on the streaming radar. Naji Marshall and PJ Washington (12 points, four rebounds and two assists) are better fantasy options until Flagg returns. 
 -  Raphielle Johnson

 Tari Eason 
 HOU

 Tari Eason provided a boost off the bench with 19 points (8-of-15 FGs), three rebounds, one steal and one block against the Hawks on Saturday.
 Eason was ejected after playing just a few minutes in the season opener and was productive off the bench against the Spurs on Friday. However, this was his best offensive performance so far. He still wasn’t able to knock down a shot from beyond the arc, but he was still able to set a season high for scoring. Plus, the defensive production was still there, as he now has five steals in three games. Eason’s role isn’t large enough for him to be a must-roster player, but he’s still capable of producing at a high level.
 -  Noah Rubin

 Naji Marshall

 Naji Marshall produced 10 points (4-of-8 FGs, 1-of- 3 FTs), four rebounds, five assists, one steal and one three-pointer in Saturday’s loss to the Spurs.
 With Kyrie Irving and Cooper Flagg unavailable, Marshall moved into the starting lineup for Saturday’s game. He took on playmaking responsibilities for large stretches of the 122-106 defeat, dishing out five of the 12 assists recorded by Mavericks starters. While Irving should be back for Monday’s game against the Heat, Flagg’s shoulder injury may keep him out for multiple games. If so, Marshall is worth streaming in deep leagues. 
 -  Raphielle Johnson

 Daniel Gafford finished Saturday’s loss to the Spurs with 12 points (6-of-9 FGs), nine rebounds, two assists, three steals and two blocked shots.
 Gafford appeared to tweak something in his lower body during the first half of Saturday’s game, but he wasn’t on the bench long before returning. The veteran center’s final line lacked only a three-pointer, but no one expects Gafford to add value in that category. After two underwhelming performances to start the season, Gafford needed a night like Saturday, as did those who still roster him. 
 -  Raphielle Johnson

 Reed Sheppard 
 HOU 
 Guard 
 #15 
 Player Stats

 Reed Sheppard started against the Hawks on Saturday and contributed 19 points (7-of-13 FGs), six rebounds, seven assists, two steals and five three-pointers.
 Fred VanVleet (knee) was sidelined for the second leg of Houston’s back-to-back, which allowed Sheppard to get the start. He took full advantage of the opportunity and made his presence felt on both ends of the floor, including some hustle plays that didn’t show up in the box score. He played well, and it resulted in an excellent night in fantasy hoops. Houston’s next back-to-back is next week, so Sheppard should get another start then.
 -  Noah Rubin

 Sergio De Larrea 
 DAL 
 Guard 
 #55 
 Player Stats
 Link copied to clipboard! 
 Sergio de Larrea tallied 21 points (9-of-15 FGs), five rebounds, four assists and three three-pointers in Saturday’s loss to the Spurs.
 De Larrea didn’t start Saturday’s game, but Kyrie Irving’s and Cooper Flagg’s absences gave the rookie opportunities he wouldn’t get if the Mavericks’ rotation were whole. To his credit, the first-round pick capitalized on the extra playing time, leading the Mavericks in points and three-pointers. De Larrea’s performance doesn’t change much regarding his value in redraft leagues, as Irving should be available for Monday’s game against the Heat. But dynasty-league managers who are rostering the rookie should be thrilled with what they saw. 
 -  Raphielle Johnson

 Stephon Castle notched 19 points (8-of-18 FGs), four rebounds, eight assists, three steals and three three-pointers in Saturday’s win over the Mavericks.
 Through three games, Castle has shot 23-of-51 (45.1%) from the field. While that isn’t great, it’s slightly higher than his career mark of 44.7%. Beyond the points, Castle offered solid assist and steal production against the Mavericks in 28 minutes. San Antonio opens Week 2 with a Tuesday/Wednesday back-to-back, so Castle’s playing time could stay in the high-20s in one of those games.
